chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Rabi' ibn Abdillah and al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said:
He said: "Look into your heart. If it rejects your companion, then one of you two has done something improper."

key_terms.أحدث: Committed something new/improper — introduced an innovation or wrongdoing
key_terms.صاحب: Companion/friend — close associate in religious fellowship
key_terms.قلب: Heart — the seat of spiritual and moral awareness in Islamic thought

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about trusting your heart regarding friendships?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that the heart serves as a moral compass in interpersonal relationships. When a person's heart turns away from a companion, it signals that one of the two has committed a wrong — either the person whose heart has changed, or the companion being judged. This teaching was directed at the early Shia community to emphasize self-examination and accountability in friendships.
